contract: Production AI Engineering Proof Contract v1

experiments.title: Risk-based routing
experiments.question: Does policy route each action by risk: automatic below the line, a human at the line, never above it?
experiments.claim: Reads, analysis and recommendations run without a human; a high-risk write waits for one; a prohibited action stays denied even after a human approves.
experiments.hypothesis: Reads, analysis and recommendations run without a human; a high-risk write waits for one; a prohibited action stays denied even after a human approves.
experiments.setup: Fresh platform per test; the payment-service incident (14% error rate after v4.18.0); prod-change-policy v7.
experiments.invariant: Every routed action ends where the policy tier says, and approval never converts DENY into ALLOW.
experiments.limitations: Deterministic suite: simulated enterprise systems, identity provider and clock; no model is called.

experiments.title: Exact-action binding
experiments.question: Does an approval authorize exactly one action and nothing adjacent to it?
experiments.claim: An approval is bound to the digest of capability, target, arguments, environment, preconditions and policy version; any change is refused or forces re-evaluation.
experiments.hypothesis: An approval is bound to the digest of capability, target, arguments, environment, preconditions and policy version; any change is refused or forces re-evaluation.
experiments.setup: Approve rollbackDeployment(payment-service, production, v4.18.0 to v4.17.2), then ask the gate to run variants of it.
experiments.invariant: A mutated action never executes under an approval for a different action; a stale approval never executes.
experiments.category: B · Exact-action binding and tamper protection
experiments.limitations: Deterministic suite: simulated enterprise systems, identity provider and clock; no model is called.

experiments.title: Approval lifecycle
experiments.question: Does the approval behave as a strict state machine?
experiments.claim: Rejected, expired and canceled proposals never execute; illegal transitions fail instead of happening.
experiments.hypothesis: Rejected, expired and canceled proposals never execute; illegal transitions fail instead of happening.
experiments.setup: Deterministic clock; proposals expire 5 minutes after creation.
experiments.invariant: Only AWAITING_APPROVAL can be decided and only APPROVED can execute; terminal states stay terminal.
experiments.limitations: Deterministic suite: simulated enterprise systems, identity provider and clock; no model is called.

experiments.title: Identity and separation of duties
experiments.question: Can only an independent, authorized human approve?
experiments.claim: The approver is the authenticated principal; agents, runtimes and anyone in the request chain cannot approve; the deployment author cannot approve its rollback.
experiments.hypothesis: The approver is the authenticated principal; agents, runtimes and anyone in the request chain cannot approve; the deployment author cannot approve its rollback.
experiments.setup: Simulated identity provider: alice and omar (production-approver), dana (production-approver, authored v4.18.0), reggie (readonly).
experiments.invariant: No decision is accepted from an unauthorized, non-human or conflicted identity, and every identity survives to the audit record.
experiments.category: D · Identity and separation of duties
experiments.limitations: Deterministic suite: simulated enterprise systems, identity provider and clock; no model is called.

experiments.title: Duplicates, idempotency and concurrency
experiments.question: Do duplicates, retries and races produce exactly one business effect?
experiments.claim: Redelivered events, repeated clicks, replayed approvals, racing decisions and lost responses never duplicate a side effect.
experiments.hypothesis: Redelivered events, repeated clicks, replayed approvals, racing decisions and lost responses never duplicate a side effect.
experiments.setup: At-least-once event delivery, browser retries, a deterministic approve/reject race, an injected lost response.
experiments.invariant: The effects ledger shows at most one rollback per approved proposal, and one terminal decision per proposal.
experiments.limitations: Deterministic suite: simulated enterprise systems, identity provider and clock; no model is called.

experiments.title: Fail-closed, adversarial and audit
experiments.question: Does the boundary hold when parts fail or the input is hostile, and can every action be reconstructed?
experiments.claim: Prompt injection, an unavailable approval service, an unavailable policy engine and a failing tool all fail closed; the audit chain reconstructs a successful rollback end to end.
experiments.hypothesis: Prompt injection, an unavailable approval service, an unavailable policy engine and a failing tool all fail closed; the audit chain reconstructs a successful rollback end to end.
experiments.setup: Injected log line claiming approval; approval service and policy engine switched off; rollout failure injected.
experiments.invariant: No gated action executes without verified policy and approval; every consequential action has a complete, intact audit chain.
experiments.limitations: Deterministic suite: simulated enterprise systems, identity provider and clock; no model is called.

experiments.title: Negative controls
experiments.question: Do the canonical tests notice when a safeguard is removed?
experiments.claim: The suite is not vacuous: removing exact-action binding or approver authentication lets an unapproved side effect through, and the tests catch it.
experiments.hypothesis: With a safeguard removed, the invariant it protects breaks and the harness still completes.
experiments.setup: The same 30 tests run twice more: once with the gate's digest binding off, once with approver authentication off (identity taken from the request).
experiments.invariant: Each protected invariant breaks cleanly (a side effect appears) and every test still completes.

experiments.title: Implementation: the HTTP surface and approval inbox
experiments.question: Does the same boundary hold through the real HTTP API a person or a client would use?
experiments.claim: Events, the inbox, decisions and the audit are served over HTTP, and the approver is the credential's principal.
experiments.hypothesis: Every call returns its expected status: refused for an unauthenticated inbox, a readonly approver and an agent claiming a human identity; accepted for the authorized human; one rollback.
experiments.setup: uv run hitl serve, driven by urllib in-process: POST /events, GET /approvals, POST /approvals/{id}/decision, GET /audit/{id}.
experiments.invariant: Each call returns the expected status and exactly one rollback follows the one valid approval.

claims.statement: Policy routes by risk: reads, analysis and recommendations run without a human, and a high-risk write waits for one.
article: Not every action needs a human

claims.statement: Approval never expands authorization: a prohibited capability stays denied after an authorized human approves it.
An approval authorizes exactly one action: changing its arguments, target, environment or capability is refused, and a changed precondition or policy forces re-evaluation.
Rejected, expired and canceled approvals never execute, and illegal state transitions fail instead of happening.
Only an authenticated, authorized and independent human can approve; the agent cannot approve its own proposal.
Every identity in the chain (invoker, agent, runtime, on-behalf-of, approver, executor) survives to the audit record.
Redelivered events, repeated clicks, replayed approvals, racing decisions and lost responses produce one business effect.
The boundary fails closed: prompt injection, an unavailable approval service, an unavailable policy engine and a failing tool never produce an unapproved effect.
A successful rollback can be reconstructed end to end from the hash-chained audit records alone.
The tests are not vacuous: with exact-action binding or approver authentication removed, an unapproved side effect gets through and the suite reports it.
The suite proves control semantics, not model judgement: the enterprise systems, identity provider and clock are simulated and no model is called.
Every canonical test passed on the published run, across all ten invariants, and each negative control lowered the pass count.

items.text: Ordered, fail-closed policy decision point (prod-change-policy v7)
Approval state machine with compare-and-set transitions in SQLite
Execution gate: digest binding, expiry, consumption, preconditions, policy version, approver role
Approver authentication and separation of duties
Idempotency keys on writes; at-least-once event dedupe
HTTP API and approval inbox (stdlib http.server), driven over real HTTP
Kubernetes deployments, logging, tracing and ITSM (hitl/enterprise.py) with an effects ledger
The identity provider (config/principals.yaml): approvers authenticate with their own credential
The clock: time moves only when a test moves it
The reasoner: a deterministic evidence correlator in place of a model
A log line that claims approval was granted and asks for immediate execution (prompt injection)
Approval service down, policy engine down, rollout failure, lost response after commit
An out-of-band deployment (v4.18.1) under a pending approval; a policy version bump
A durable workflow engine for long approval pauses (Temporal, Step Functions)
Out-of-band approver authentication (OIDC CIBA) and transaction-bound authorization (OAuth RAR)
Multi-agent approval chains and AI control plane integration
